title: One-word 'Rollback' spelling is not parsed as a rollback request and the run finishes
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; no receipts; TriagePolicy; scripted model replies: a recent_deploys tool_proposal then an answer citing r1
input: Rollback the latest checkout deployment.
expected: Same write disposition as 'Roll back the latest checkout deployment.': requested_writes non-empty and a held_for_approval receipt. The run must not end finished with action record 'no side effect was requested'.
justification: Both spellings are the same English imperative. The parser's own docstring says non-matching text should yield 'no authority (the write would be rejected, never run)' (incident_env.py:198-199), but for this input no receipt is produced at all, so the disposition is silently lost. Spelling coverage is a parser-vocabulary question; the silent finish is the defect.
existing_coverage: write_retractions:8-16 tests 'roll back'/'revert' only; no test for 'Rollback'. No test asserts a run-level outcome for an unparsed write.
oracle_confidence: medium (spelling part: NEEDS_SPECIFICATION for vocabulary); high for 'no silent finish with action record none requested'
observed: requested_writes: frozenset() vs frozenset({('rollback_deploy','checkout')}) for 'Roll back'. Run status 'finished'; action record 'no side effect was requested or executed'. The 'Roll back' spelling gives status 'held' and HELD_FOR_APPROVAL. Two spellings, opposite terminal outcomes.

title: Compound rollback request loses every target after the first
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; no receipts
input: Roll back checkout and payments.
relevant_contract: CONTRACTS.md 3.1: parser matches only the first 'roll back <service>' per sentence (incident_env.py:207, :212-219)
expected: requested_writes equals the split form 'Roll back checkout. Roll back payments.', i.e. both targets. Any target not requested must not be silently omitted from the disposition.
justification: Metamorphic: splitting one sentence into two must not change the set of named targets. The parser uses re.search, which returns only the first match per clause, so the second target is discarded with no receipt or hold.
source_ref: examples/architecture/incident_env.py:205-219 (re.finditer over clauses, then one _ROLLBACK_REQUEST.search per clause); probe test_adv002
existing_coverage: write_retractions has no compound case. safety_gates:136-152 covers DIRECT/FINISH against one recognised write only.
oracle_confidence: medium-high (metamorphic oracle; the parser's documented rule is 'the next word is a service', which this input breaks, so the parser scope is a specification question but the silent drop is not)

title: FINISH accepts an answer claiming a completed rollback when wording avoids the keyword screen
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; executed service_health receipt r1 for checkout (valid status evidence); no write requested
input: Candidate answers (cite r1): 'I rolled checkout back to d-141, and it is healthy now.' / 'I have executed the rollback of checkout; it is healthy now.' / 'Checkout was restored to d-141 and is healthy now.' / 'I undid the checkout deploy; it is healthy now.' / 'I switched checkout back to build d-141; it is healthy.'
expected: host_validates(FINISH) returns False for each claim: a completed side effect is asserted and the action record shows no executed write.
justification: turnwise_core.py:543-544 says any mention of a completed side effect is refused unless a host receipt shows an executed write. The regex only matches 'rolled back|reverted|paged', 'rollback|revert' near 'done|executed|...', so these synonyms and word orders pass. The host then reports 'finished' with action record 'no side effect was requested'. The control phrase 'I rolled back checkout' is correctly rejected.
existing_coverage: safety_gates has no claim-screen case; architecture_core:252-256 covers five phrasings (rolled back, rollback complete, reverted, rolled-back, Rollback executed). Synonyms and split word order are not covered.
oracle_confidence: high (the code's own stated rule, and the claim is factually a side-effect claim)
observed: all 5 non-control phrasings accepted (the control 'I rolled back checkout' is rejected as expected); each accepted run's action record says 'no side effect was requested or executed'.

relevant_contract: CONTRACTS.md 8.2 and incident_env.py:77-79, :85-89, :278-279 (no role check when the regex does not match); 9 D9

justification: Two paraphrases of the same checkout-specific question get different host verdicts. A is rejected (missing symptom:checkout, change:checkout). B is accepted, because 'increase' is not in _CAUSAL_QUESTION and missing_evidence returns () for a task without a role regex. The _check_finish message itself names 'task-scoped' evidence as the requirement.

oracle_confidence: medium (the metamorphic equality is sound; whether 'Did ... increase' is causal is a specification question, but a checkout answer citing only payments evidence is not task-scoped under the code's own message)

'start' matches the incident_start cue, so a yes/no comparison is answered with a timestamp. The run then ends answered_directly with a record that does not answer the question. Confidence is medium because the authors' intent for mixed-subject questions is stated only in the comment.

title: Raw HTTP 429 from a non-ledger model port is retried by the policy until the model budget is gone
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; Budget(max_model_calls=4); ScriptedPort raises an exception with status_code=429 (not a ModelCallFailed); no ProviderLedger
input: Is checkout healthy right now? (status intent; the first model call follows one read)
relevant_contract: CONTRACTS.md 7 (turnwise_core.py:362-382, :370; describe_failure :520-521); 9 D10; AGENTS 'first-429 stop' (paid path uses ProviderLedger and classify_from_wire, provider.py:284-302)
expected: After the first HTTP 429, the policy issues no further model call (policies.py:74-75 intends this).
justification: rate_limited is set only when the exception is a ModelCallFailed with the 429 category (turnwise_core.py:370). A raw error with status_code 429 is categorised as 'provider error HTTP 429' by describe_failure but does not set the flag, so the policy's rate-limit HOLD never fires and each outcome is 'invalid'. Scope: the real paid path wraps 429 through the ledger, so this is a policy-layer gap on non-ledger ports, not a paid-call exposure.
existing_coverage: provider_readiness:607-617 tests the transport stop (ledger). No test drives the policy with a raw 429 exception.
oracle_confidence: medium-high for the policy-layer intent; low severity because the paid path is protected elsewhere
observed: 4 model calls; every outcome kind 'invalid' with provider_rate_limited=False; run ends 'held' only after the model budget is exhausted.

title: Paraphrases of one diagnostic question get different first decisions: deterministic read vs heavy model
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; no receipts; no services gap (checkout named)
input: Did the checkout deploy cause the errors? / Did the checkout deployment increase error rates?
relevant_contract: CONTRACTS.md 5 and 6; policies.py:23 (_DIAGNOSTIC), :103-109 (cheap evidence first), :111-122 (heavy model); incident_env.py:77-79 (separate causal vocabulary); 9 D8
expected: Same first decision for both paraphrases; the 'cause' phrasing and the 'increase' phrasing should both start with a deterministic evidence read.
justification: 'cause' matches _DIAGNOSTIC, so the policy reads error_trend first. 'increase' matches neither _DIAGNOSTIC nor _STATUS, so intent is 'other', no evidence is read, and the policy calls the heavy model with empty context. This is an unnecessary model invocation, and the two keyword vocabularies in one file disagree. Expected-behaviour detail is a specification choice, but equality of paraphrases is not.
existing_coverage: No paraphrase test for routing. policies tests (architecture_core) not re-audited for this wording.

title: A self-contradicting same-turn instruction is turned into a rollback approval request
initial_state: Canonical IncidentHost; no receipts
input: Roll back checkout. Never roll back checkout.
relevant_contract: CONTRACTS.md 3.1 and 9 D6: incident_env.py:173-174 says 'mixed instructions may need clarification, not approval'
expected: requested_writes is empty (no approval request). Clarification or a neutral disposition is acceptable; an approval hold for checkout is not.
justification: The parser checks only the listed withdrawal phrases. 'Never roll back checkout.' is a negated sentence, so it is excluded from the count, but the first, positive sentence still produces an approval request. The code's own comment says same-turn mixed instructions should not be approved.
existing_coverage: write_retractions:28-42 covers withdrawals in the list only (e.g. 'Actually, no', 'Never mind'). 'Never roll back X' is not in the list and is not tested.
oracle_confidence: medium-high (oracle is the code's own comment)
observed: requested_writes -> {('rollback_deploy','checkout')}; the run would present an approval hold for checkout (OBS-C).
